headline: US admits for the first time it has weapons in space
summary: Air Force Secretary Troy Meink said Monday the US military has "on orbit, space-control weapons," the first time an official has said so. Officials gave no details of what the weapon does. The Space Force's new chief said Chinese and Russian anti-satellite advances made it time to say it. Russia and China warned of an arms race.

cover_question.q: Is there a war in space?

cover_answer: No. Nobody is fighting up there. It guards satellites.
table_question: Does showing your weapon make a fight more or less likely?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The United States said it has a weapon up in space, where the satellites are. Satellites are machines that circle the Earth, and the military uses them to see and to talk. The weapon is there to guard them, like a fence around a playground. Nobody is fighting up there, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: A guard for the machines in the sky is enough. Nothing has happened, and nothing is coming here.

8-12.script: The US said for the first time it has a weapon in orbit. Its Space Force chief says China and Russia built tools that can grab a satellite and drag it to a new orbit, so the US needs a way to defend its own. Like a bike lock: you buy one when others start carrying bolt cutters.
8-12.why: They built grabbers, so we built guards. Does that ever end?

13-17.script: Are we going to have a war in space? The US just admitted it has a weapon in orbit and says China and Russia can already grab satellites. Its general calls the goal deterrence "from a position of strength." Is announcing a weapon a warning or a dare?
13-17.why: Deterrence is a bet teens can weigh. Let them go first.

5-7.q: Is there a war in space?
5-7.a: No. Nobody is fighting up there. The US says it has a weapon to protect its satellites, and some other countries are grumbling about it.

8-12.a: Officials won't say what it is. The Space Force chief says it can defend satellites from attack, and that it was time to admit it exists.
The general says it was time to say it once China and Russia showed they can grab satellites and move them. The details are still secret.

13-17.q: Are we going to have a war in space?
13-17.a: Nobody is fighting there. The Space Force says the weapon exists to deter attacks on satellites. Russia and China call it the start of an arms race.
The Pentagon is asking Congress for $71.3 billion for the Space Force this year, the biggest one-year jump for a service since 1952, by percentage.
